name: How much does a home addition permit cost in Los Angeles area cities?

mainEntity.name: What drives the total permit cost for a home addition in Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, or Burbank?
mainEntity.text: What drives the total permit cost for a home addition in Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, or Burbank?

acceptedAnswer.text: The total permitting cost for a home addition is usually more than a single filing fee. Costs often include a plan check fee, building permit fee, and separate trade permits for plumbing, electrical, and mechanical work. Some projects also trigger demolition fees, grading-related fees, or outside-agency review costs. Larger additions generally cost more because permit fees are often tied to valuation, scope, and complexity. In Pasadena and other cities with more detailed submittal standards, the cost can rise if revised plan check rounds are needed. Homeowners should also account for document preparation costs such as drafting, engineering, Title 24 compliance, and surveys, because those are frequently necessary to get the permit approved. The best budgeting approach is to ask the local building counter what fees apply to the exact scope, not just the addition size.
acceptedAnswer.description: Permit cost is usually based on project valuation, square footage, and the number of reviews or trade permits required. The total can include plan check fees, building permit fees, energy review costs, demolition permits, and separate plumbing, electrical, or mechanical permits. Complex additions generally cost more to permit than simple ones.
